insight: ingredients.js PAC/POD derivation ANDs a validity check across 7 sugars including galactose; USDA routinely reports only 5 (no galactose), so the gate almost always fails and PAC/POD are silently left unpopulated. Treat absent galactose/maltose as 0, not as invalid.

The sugar to PAC/POD formula exists twice: ingredients.js:781 takes fractions (0-1), tools.js:174 takes percents (0-100). Same math, 100x apart. Change one and the PAC/POD calculator silently disagrees with the USDA importer.

office-hours Phase 5 writes {user}-{branch}-design-*.md with the raw branch name, so a branch containing / creates a subdirectory. plan-eng-review sanitizes / to - and globs flat, so it reports No design doc found. Write the design doc with the branch slashes already replaced by dashes.

npm test runs node test-app.js, a 1624-line custom Playwright harness with 24 methods and 116 logTest assertions, all via page.evaluate against a live server. testNoConsoleErrors filters type===error only, so console.log spam passes. No pure-function unit lane exists.

CORRECTS usda-pacpod-galactose-gate. The PAC/POD gate fails because of nutrient NAME mismatches, not galactose coverage. FDC returns Glucose (not Glucose (dextrose)) and Total Sugars (not Sugars, Total NLEA). getNutritionValue returns -1 on no match and fails silently, so Sugar never populated either. Measured 0/11 pass with current names, 6/11 with corrected names.

To decide whether an incomplete FDC sugar breakdown is safe to derive from, sum the individual sugars present and compare to Total Sugars. If it reconciles within tolerance the absent sugars are genuinely zero (honey reconciles to 0.03g while reporting no lactose). Beats any hardcoded safely-zero sugar list: self-validating, no chemistry table to maintain.

FDC Foundation records carry Water/Fat/Energy but no individual sugars and no Total Sugars. SR Legacy carries the full sugar profile. ingredients.js:714-735 prefers Foundation, so for formulation it selects the record that cannot produce PAC/POD.

gstack _gstack_codex_auth_probe reports AUTH_OK and CODEX_MODE: ready whenever OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY is merely non-empty. Codex CLI 0.147 does NOT read those env vars: it needs the key stored via `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key`, which writes ~/.codex/auth.json. With the var set but no login, codex returns 401 Missing bearer or basic authentication in header while the probe still says ready. Smoke test with a trivial `codex exec` before trusting the probe.

~/.codex/auth.json is container-local in Claude Code on the web, so codex authentication does not survive container recreation even when OPENAI_API_KEY is set in the environment config. The SessionStart hook must re-run codex login on every cold start.

/review SKILL.md reads .claude/skills/review/checklist.md, but in a symlinked install ~/.claude/skills/review/ contains only a SKILL.md symlink. The real files (checklist.md, greptile-triage.md, design-checklist.md, specialists/) live at ~/.claude/skills/gstack/review/. Read from there instead of stopping on the missing path.

IceEd.html is a frozen 3528-line snapshot of the original monolithic app (documented as a backup in STRUCTURE.md, STACK.md and MODULARIZATION_PLAN.md). It carries its own copy of the ingredient data, the Sugars table and the USDA import, so any fix in js/ leaves it stale. Do not patch it: it is a historical record. Check STACK.md deployment claims instead.

Async hooks are configured with an "async": true FIELD on the hook handler in .claude/settings.json, plus "timeout". Printing {"async": true, "asyncTimeout": N} from the hook script does NOTHING -- the script stays synchronous and the JSON is just stray stdout. Also set a "matcher" (e.g. "startup"): with no matcher a SessionStart hook fires on startup, resume, clear, compact AND fork, so expensive setup re-runs mid-session. gstack office-hours/session-start templates teach the stdout-JSON pattern, which is wrong. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

Do not use Math.max to pick between alias nutrient names in the USDA import. getNutritionValue scans foods in Foundation > SR Legacy > Survey order and returns the first match, so each single name already respects record priority. Math.max across aliases picks the numerically larger value regardless of which record it came from, so one ingredient profile can be assembled from two different USDA records. Use ordered first-match (firstNutritionValue) instead.

When falling back across alias names AND across priority-ordered records, the loop nesting decides correctness. Records must be the OUTER loop and aliases the INNER loop. Alias-outer looks equivalent but exhausts every record for the first alias before trying the second, so a lower-priority record matching the primary name beats a higher-priority record matching the alias. Caught by cross-model review after a first fix got the nesting backwards.

Validating a numeric shell input with ^[0-9]+$ is not enough: a value like 999999999999999999999999999999 matches but overflows bash signed 64-bit arithmetic, so every [ -ge ] errors with integer expression expected and a bounded wait loop becomes infinite. Bound the digit count and range-check.

Do not validate a shell variable with grep -qE. grep matches LINE BY LINE, so a multiline value like $(printf "1\ninvalid") passes on its first line. Use a case statement, which matches the whole string: case "$v" in ""|*[!0-9]*) reject;; esac. Also bound magnitude BEFORE arithmetic (long digit strings overflow bash 64-bit ints and make every -ge error), and strip leading zeros so 00000 is understood as 0. This defect recurred three times in one session, each time in a different form.

Iterated cross-model adversarial review on this branch converged 5 -> 3 -> 3 -> 0 findings across four passes. Passes 2 and 3 were essential: two pass-2 findings were defects the pass-1 fixes introduced, and pass 3 caught the third variant of a bug fixed twice. Re-running after each fix round is worth it until a pass comes back clean; a single pass would have left five P1s partly unfixed and two new ones added.

Stating a decision in three sections of a design doc (Scope, Correction narrative, Implementation Tasks) guarantees drift: when measurement changed the design, two of three got updated and six passages were left describing abandoned approaches, including one instructing a future implementer to use the exact pattern a later review had removed. Make ONE section authoritative for buildable detail (the task list), keep rationale separate, and freeze dated correction narratives as never-edit.

A single percent-populated success criterion becomes unevaluable the moment a feature can produce estimated values: the same implementation scored 91% counting estimates and 73% excluding them. Split into measured-rate and derived-rate, and treat the gap (estimate rate) as a watched signal rather than a target, so the metric cannot be passed by guessing more.

This repo has no VERSION file and versions via package.json semver (3-digit). gstack-version-bump classify therefore returns DRIFT_UNEXPECTED, whose documented handling is STOP-and-reconcile. That is a false positive: there is nothing to reconcile, the repo simply never adopted the 4-digit scheme. Bump package.json directly and continue. Decided 2026-08-11 to keep one version source.
